label: rem:ohtsuki-tower-bar-parity
title: Bar-parity of the Ohtsuki tower at the imaginary substrate: even rungs are $\mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak{V}$ (mass), odd rungs are $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}$ (the bar-odd $S$)
html:
Remark. Bar-parity of the Ohtsuki tower at the imaginary substrate: even rungs are \mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak{V} (mass), odd rungs are \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} (the bar-odd S)

The identification of the bar-odd S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / E_0 with the decay projection \mathrm{Im}(q) (candidate (iii); rem:c3-s-imq-decay-projection) has a clean structural counterpart at the level of the figure-eight complex volume \mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS}. The finite-b (one-loop-plus-corrections) expansion is the Ohtsuki tower

  \mathfrak{V}_b = \mathfrak{V}_0 + \sum_{n \geq 1} \kappa_n\,(2\pi b^2)^n,

with real coefficients \kappa_n \in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{3})\cdot\pi^{\lceil n/2\rceil} (for instance \kappa_1 = 11\sqrt{3}\,\pi/108 and \kappa_2 = 2\pi^2/27). At the substrate the fluctuation variable is imaginary: with b = \sqrt{\log q_0 / 2\pi}\,e^{i\pi/4} one has 2\pi b^2 = i\,t, where t = \log q_0 \in \mathbb{R}.

The imaginary substrate direction splits the tower by parity, and the split is exactly the \mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS} decomposition. Since (i\,t)^2 = -t^2 is real, pairing the imaginary factors gives:

  • even rungs are real — \mathrm{Im}\big((i\,t)^{2m}\,\kappa\big) = 0, so the even sub-tower feeds \mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol}, the bar-even (mass) face;
  • odd rungs are imaginary — \mathrm{Re}\big((i\,t)^{2m+1}\,\kappa\big) = 0, so the odd sub-tower feeds \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{CS}, the bar-odd S (decay) face.

Both statements are proved sorry-free over \mathbb{C} in the Lean file OhtsukiTowerBarParity.lean (even_rung_real, odd_rung_imaginary), with the concrete leading rungs \kappa_1 (odd, imaginary) and \kappa_2 (even, real) as instances.

The consequence for the c₃ wall is that the bar-odd S — hence its anchor-dependent sign-flip — lives entirely in the odd (imaginary) sub-tower; the even sub-tower is the anchor-blind volume/mass channel. The odd sub-tower is factorially divergent (Gevrey-1), and its Borel–Padé resummation at the imaginary substrate is single-valued: the Borel singularity sits at the real action A = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\pi \approx 0.646 (the geometric-to-conjugate saddle gap), off the imaginary integration ray, so there is no Stokes ambiguity and no exponentially small trans-series. Resurgence therefore returns the exact smooth \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} \approx 0.055 together with the action cross-check, but supplies no anchor-dependent piece. This confirms, from the resummation side, that the S sign-flip is the 1/u^3 ladder representation of a smooth object rather than a physical singularity (compare rem:c3-s-imq-decay-projection); the resummation is recorded in qbeta_c3_borel_pade_resummation_probe.py.

A second, distinct instance of the same bar-parity principle — the deuteron binding. The rung-parity split above is one realisation of "bar involution splits the object by parity"; the deuteron binding correction realises the same principle on a different object — the Frobenius-paired Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_D) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash 6} w_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda_q(\beta_D) over the eleven Wedderburn blocks of H_6(q) (not the figure-eight complex-volume tower). Here the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} acts on the per-block term T_\lambda(q) = w_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda_q(\beta_D) by a signed partition conjugation \lambda \mapsto \lambda' (Young-diagram transpose). Three exact facts pin it: the Markov weight is conjugation-invariant, w_\lambda(q) = w_{\lambda'}(q) (the hook multiset is preserved under transpose); partition conjugation is the bar involution on characters, \chi^{\lambda'}(\beta_D; q) = \chi^\lambda(\beta_D; q^{-1}) (verified against the derived q_0/q_0^{-1} caches); and the weight carries its own bar-sign w_\lambda(q^{-1}) = (-1)^{n-1} w_\lambda(q) from the (q-q^{-1})^{n-1} prefactor. Together these give T_\lambda(q^{-1}) = (-1)^{n-1} T_{\lambda'}(q), and for the deuteron n = 6 the sign is (-1)^5 = -1. For n = 6 the eleven partitions form five conjugate pairs plus the single self-conjugate (3,2,1), and — because of that -1 — the self-conjugate block is bar-odd: T_{(3,2,1)}(q^{-1}) = -T_{(3,2,1)}(q), so it contributes only to the bar-odd impurity t, never to the bar-even coefficient g_2. Equivalently, g_2 is carried by the conjugate-pair asymmetries \Delta_\lambda - \Delta_{\lambda'} (which vanish on the self-conjugate), and t by the pair-symmetric parts plus (3,2,1). The parity backbone is proved sorry-free over a generic commutative ring in ConjugationParitySplit.lean (selfConj_barEven_zero_deuteron, pEven_conj, pEven_selfConj); the derivation establishes the structure (signed parity) of the correction only — the per-partition \Delta_\lambda magnitudes remain the open Track-A gate.
